data.title: Injection corpus runner: per-case protocol floor from IDL @since; signing-wire probes become ordinary cases

data.body:
[risk:high][review-summary] No blocking finding in the persisted range.

Failure modes: An IDL floor can be missed, a request can use a version below its operation floor, a signing-wire operation can stop before admission, or coverage can omit a privileged operation. The independent IDL scan at lines 1949-1988, request selection at 2126-2127, admission assertions at 2473-2501, and coverage closure at 3059-3083 fail closed for these cases.

Edge cases: Known operations without @since resolve to 3.0; unknown operations panic; all six protocol-3.8 operations use separate 3.8 fixtures; and the four bodies without free text use explicit PrivilegeProbe carriage.

Rollback: Revert commit 683000545d10601e169572ba6e41ee79e0bb7a7a. This restores the fixed 3.2 corpus fixture and bespoke 3.8 probes. No product state or schema migration needs reversal.

Monitoring: Treat failures in the five protocol-floor tests, enforcement::the_privilege_bit_is_the_only_difference_between_admitted_and_denied, or the privileged-operation coverage test as security evidence regressions.

Validation: I reviewed the complete 27d378b9b243f8e893b3f0c441252409ded6895c..683000545d10601e169572ba6e41ee79e0bb7a7a range. I traced the IDL parser, handshake, request envelope, registry version gate, dispatch admission record, and acceptance re-derivation. I did not run tests because this reviewer may write only Seal metadata.

data.reason: Informational risk-high review summary; no action required.
Whole persisted range reviewed. No blocking security finding. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.
